subject: PrivDeploy pricing: volume-triggered discounts & SLA carve-outs
messages:
From: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@bluebridge.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Chan <tom.chan@bluebridge.ai>
Date: 2026-07-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PrivDeploy commercial options

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. BlueBridge is lining up procurement and engineering for a potential Q4 Private deployment (VPC) and we need clarity on two things before our internal approval:

1) Can we structure discounts that kick in based on monthly committed GPU-hours (a three-tier volume trigger)?
2) Is the platform fee negotiable for a 6-month pilot (we'd like a reduced platform fee for pilot + observability addon as an optional paid extra).

Our legal team also asked for a sample SOW and a ballpark on any credits for missed SLA during onboarding. Can you share the simplest structure that would speed approvals on our side?

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Torres
Head of Cloud Services, BlueBridge AI
alicia.torres@bluebridge.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy commercial options

Hi Alicia —

Thanks for the clear ask. High-level answers up front, then I attached a short concession matrix and SOW skeleton for review.

- Volume-triggered discounts: yes, we can do a 3-tier structure (pilot, production baseline, scale). Discounts are applied to per-token inference charge and operator license line; platform fee can be tiered as well.
- Pilot platform fee: we can offer a temporary reduced platform fee for a 6-month pilot, linked to a pilot acceptance milestone. Observability addon can be optional, billed monthly, or included at a discounted rate as part of an onboarding bundle.
- SLA credits during onboarding: we have a standard onboarding SLA credit table; for pilot customers we typically provide a capped implementation credit tied to milestone acceptance (see attached).

Next steps I recommend:
- Internal pricing review (Marissa) to confirm concession sizing against deal economics.
- Legal to get the SOW skeleton and propose any contract carve-outs (David is copied).
- If you can share an expected monthly GPU-hour range for pilot + projected scale, I will get a tailored concession table back within 48 hours.

I attached: privdeploy_concession_table_v1.xlsx (workback), SOW-draft-v0.2.docx, and a one-page pricing_and_sla_note.

Would you be available for a 30-min call Thursday to walk through the triggers?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Director, Enterprise Sales — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-07-26T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: BlueBridge concession framing

Kim / David —

Quick internal note after reviewing Alicia's ask and the initial numbers:

- Pilot (first 6 months): offer 25% off platform fee and 10% off operator license; cap implementation credit at $30k tied to onboarding acceptance (milestone-based).
- Baseline (committed monthly GPU-hours between 1k-5k): 15% discount on per-token line + 10% platform fee reduction compared to list.
- Scale (5k+ GPU-hours): 25% per-token discount + 20% off operator license; there should be a midpoint review after 3 months of scale usage to adjust commit.

Observability addon: recommend we offer as paid addon at 50% discount for pilot if they commit to baseline.

Legal/ops flags:
- Avoid open-ended SLA credits; use defined credit bands.
- We should include a rollback clause if usage drops >40% for two consecutive months.

I'll prepare a short concession table (attached) and a one-pager justification for leadership approval.

Marissa
VP, Commercial Strategy
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Kimberly / Marissa —

Thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifications from procurement/legal:

- The $30k implementation credit sounds reasonable, but legal wants the mechanics spelled out (how credits are calculated, outage definitions, and cap).
- For the volume tiers, can discounts be automated (i.e., applied on invoice when thresholds are crossed) rather than retroactive true-ups? Procurement prefers forward-looking tiers.
- Observability: our engineering lead wants to trial the addon during pilot but only if it's included at no additional cost for the first 45 days. Is that doable?

Timeline: procurement needs final commercial terms and SOW by Aug 5 to hit our September board approval. If you can deliver a final concession table and SOW with the credit mechanics described, we'll route to legal the same day.

Also, Tom (cc) will be our procurement lead for the contract negotiation. He may loop in finance for invoicing cadence.

Best,
Alicia

Subject: Re: PrivDeploy commercial options — proposed final structure

Hi Alicia / Tom —

Appreciate the timeline. Attached is an updated concession table and a redlined SOW that explicitly calls out the credit mechanics and invoice treatment. Highlights:

- Implementation credit: capped at $30,000; credit is issued as a service credit applied to the first full invoice after final onboarding acceptance. Credit triggers: documented onboarding milestone misses (list in SOW).
- Volume tiers (forward-looking, non-retroactive): discounts apply to the invoice period following the month the threshold is reached. Example: if monthly GPU-hours exceed Tier 2 threshold in June, the July invoice reflects Tier 2 pricing.
- Pilot observability: we can include the observability addon free for the first 45 days of the pilot, provided you sign the pilot SOW and accept the pilot acceptance criteria. After 45 days it will bill at the agreed addon rate or be removed.
- Rollback / churn protection: there's an automatic review clause after 3 months of scale where both parties can rebaseline commit levels; if usage falls below 60% of committed baseline for 2 months, platform fee reverts to list minus a 5% grace discount.

Deliverables attached: privdeploy_concession_table_v1.xlsx (v2 with numbers filled), SOW-draft-v0.2.docx (redlined), privdeploy_pricing_and_sla_note.pdf (summary).

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the pilot GPU-hour estimate (range ok) by Jul 30.
2) We finalize concession numbers and I route to Finance for invoicing cadence (monthly in arrears vs monthly advanced).
3) Legal review of SOW; we'll accept reasonable redlines that don't expand credit scope.

If you’d like, I can set up a call with David (legal) and Marissa (commercial) on Friday to clear any procurement items so you can meet Aug 5.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
